text: SO THAT the Quraysh might remain secure,<sup foot_note=106001>1</sup>

foot_notes.106001: Lit., "for the safeguarding of the Quraysh", i.e., as the custodians of the Kabah and the tribe in the midst of which the Last Prophet, Muhammad, was to appear. Thus, the "security of the Quraysh" is a metonym for the security of the Kabah, the focal point of the Faith based on the concept of God's oneness, for the sake of which the army of Abrahah was destroyed (see introductory note as well as preceding surah).

text: secure in their winter and summer journeys,<sup foot_note=106002>2</sup>

foot_notes.106002: I.e., the two annual trade caravans—to the Yemen in winter and to Syria in summer—on which the prosperity of Mecca depended.

text: Let them, therefore, worship the Sustainer of this Temple;<sup foot_note=106003>3</sup>
who has given them food against hunger, and made them safe from danger.<sup foot_note=106004>4</sup>

foot_notes.106004: Cf. Abraham's prayer, "O my Sustainer! Make this a land secure, and grant its people fruitful sustenance" (2:126).
